review.decision: Protect managed ownership without granting input from an expired heartbeat; recover only when independent receipts prove the legacy index belongs to another pane.
review.notes: Reviewed the installed incident shape and the shared publication lease. Use the real store, fake process and terminal probes, and a synthetic HOME. Cover missing and unverified evidence plus recovery after a partial write. The definite writer of the historical incident remains unknown. These cases do not certify deployed UI or production changes.

cases.description: Legacy publishers preserve an expired but potentially owned frontend index
cases.setup: Synthetic private state with an expired managed incumbent and controlled process status.
cases.action: Attempt a foreign-thread hook Save and the publication entry shared by process fallback and bootstrap, then exercise same-owner update and confirmed retirement.
cases.expected: An expired receipt confers no live authority. Foreign and unknown producer attempts leave the exact incumbent in place, same-owner update retains its frontend identity, and a positively gone or retired owner permits normal legacy publication.

cases.description: Current bridge restores a known cross-pane conflict with original bytes preserved
cases.setup: Strict current frontend and independent native receipts for two distinct panes sharing the same backend; the incumbent is a legacy index containing extra forward-compatible fields.
cases.action: Run the real heartbeat and inspect the recovered live index, native receipt, foreign pane record and private archive; inject an index publish failure and retry.
cases.expected: Only the exact original thread regains live identity. The other pane is unchanged. The archive preserves the exact displaced bytes and is reused on retry; a failed index write does not lose the original or prevent a verified retry.

cases.description: Unproven conflicts remain unchanged with a typed diagnostic
cases.setup: Synthetic cases vary independent receipts, same pane, managed conflicting index, unsafe file or archive, and newer publisher.
cases.action: Attempt recovery from the original bridge and inspect the index and frontend receipt.
cases.expected: No recovery or input authority; a stable typed reason distinguishes conflict from unavailable preservation. Exact existing bytes and the producer receipt are preserved.
